editorialDraft.en: Before the 1955 reform, the Vigil of Pentecost included six prophetic readings and the blessing of baptismal water, echoing Holy Saturday. Those older ceremonies should not be confused with the order followed in 1962.
editorialDraft.fr: Avant la réforme de 1955, la vigile de la Pentecôte comportait six prophéties et la bénédiction de l’eau baptismale, en écho au Samedi saint. Il ne faut pas confondre ces anciens rites avec l’ordo suivi en 1962.

humanReviewRecords.needsVerification: Pre-1955 rites cannot be presented as the 1962 sequence; separate pre-reform and 1962 states.

editorialDraft.en: The Wednesday Ember Day within Pentecost week traditionally has its Roman station at Saint Mary Major. Its readings associate the gift of the Holy Ghost, apostolic witness and Christ as the bread of life; the Ember observance also recalls prayer for ordinands.
editorialDraft.fr: Le mercredi des Quatre-Temps de la Pentecôte a traditionnellement sa station romaine à Sainte-Marie-Majeure. Ses lectures rapprochent le don du Saint-Esprit, le témoignage apostolique et le Christ, pain de vie ; ces Quatre-Temps sont aussi liés à la prière pour les ordinands.

humanReviewRecords.needsVerification: Cross-check the exact 1962 Proper and station in canonical owner; distinguish historic ordinations from current practice.

humanReviewRecords.sourceTitle: Immaculée Conception de la Vierge Marie
humanReviewRecords.sourcePanelLocator: ICRSP page Commentaires; see subject notes
humanReviewRecords.observedClaim: Earlier Mass adapted from Nativity of the Virgin; post-1854 new office/Missal texts; Vigil and octave removed in 1955
humanReviewRecords.comparisonToCurrentApp: Owner files inspected; exact canonical target record ID not yet certified, do not mint an ID

editorialDraft.en: The liturgical celebration of the Immaculate Conception developed over several centuries. Earlier texts drew on the Nativity of Mary; a distinct office and Mass followed the proclamation of the dogma, while the former vigil and octave disappeared from the 1962 calendar.
editorialDraft.fr: La célébration liturgique de l’Immaculée Conception s’est développée au fil des siècles. Les anciens textes reprenaient ceux de la Nativité de Marie ; un office et une messe propres suivirent la proclamation du dogme, tandis que l’ancienne vigile et l’octave ne figurent plus au calendrier de 1962.

humanReviewRecords.needsVerification: Do not re-add suppressed vigil/octave to universal 1962 calendar; exact historical description needs independent corroboration.

humanReviewRecords.sourcePanelLocator: ICRSP page Commentaires; see subject notes
humanReviewRecords.observedClaim: 1847 universal extension of Patronage feast; 1870 elevation; 1913 Wednesday transfer; 1955 suppression and May 1 Joseph Worker
humanReviewRecords.comparisonToCurrentApp: Owner files inspected; exact canonical target record ID not yet certified, do not mint an ID

editorialDraft.en: An older feast of Saint Joseph as Patron of the Universal Church developed during the nineteenth century and was later assigned to a Wednesday after Easter. Its movable celebration was removed in 1955, when the feast of Saint Joseph the Worker on 1 May was introduced.
editorialDraft.fr: Une ancienne fête de saint Joseph, Patron de l’Église universelle, se développa au XIXe siècle et fut ensuite fixée à un mercredi du temps pascal. Cette célébration mobile fut supprimée en 1955, lors de l’institution de la fête de saint Joseph Artisan au 1er mai.

humanReviewRecords.needsVerification: Do not reinstate older movable patronage feast into 1962 universal cycle; source has 1969 polemical opinion separately.

humanReviewRecords.comparisonToCurrentApp: Owner files inspected; exact canonical target record ID not yet certified, do not mint an ID

editorialDraft.en: The cult of Saints Gervasius and Protasius spread from Milan after Saint Ambrose reported the discovery of their relics in 386. Historical Roman references also associate their veneration with the church later known as San Vitale.
editorialDraft.fr: Le culte des saints Gervais et Protais se répandit depuis Milan après la découverte de leurs reliques rapportée par saint Ambroise en 386. Des témoignages romains anciens relient aussi leur vénération à l’église connue plus tard sous le nom de San Vitale.

humanReviewRecords.needsVerification: Before user-facing biography verify St Ambrose own source, competing archaeological chronology, and exact location IDs.

humanReviewRecords.comparisonToCurrentApp: Owner files inspected; exact canonical target record ID not yet certified, do not mint an ID

editorialDraft.en: Gaudete, the Third Sunday of Advent, takes its name from the opening word of the Introit. Its joyful character is traditionally marked by rose vestments where used, and the Roman station is associated with Saint Peter's Basilica.
editorialDraft.fr: Gaudete, le troisième dimanche de l’Avent, tire son nom du premier mot de l’introït. Son caractère joyeux s’exprime traditionnellement, là où cet usage est observé, par les ornements roses ; la station romaine est associée à la basilique Saint-Pierre.

humanReviewRecords.needsVerification: Check optionality and source era before describing as binding liturgical instructions; avoid anti-other-confessions polemics.

editorialDraft.en: The feast of All Saints has several historical strands, including the dedication of the Roman Pantheon to Saint Mary and the Martyrs. Earlier calendars also included a penitential vigil on 31 October, which was suppressed before the 1962 Missal.
editorialDraft.fr: La Toussaint possède plusieurs racines historiques, dont la dédicace du Panthéon de Rome à Sainte-Marie-et-aux-Martyrs. Les anciens calendriers prévoyaient également une vigile pénitentielle le 31 octobre, supprimée avant le missel de 1962.

humanReviewRecords.needsVerification: Avoid single-origin claims, date of Roman feast contested; distinguish today's 1962 Mass from pre-1955 vigil and fast.
